question: The Golden Temple, which is situated in Amritsar, Punjab, is alternatively known as _____. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Akal Takht
Anandpur Sahib
Sri Harmandir Sahib
Gurudwara Hemkunt Sahib
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sri Harmandir Sahib

Explanation:
The Golden Temple, located in Amritsar, Punjab, is officially known as Sri Harmandir Sahib. It was built in 1604 by Guru Arjan Dev Ji. 'Harmandir' means 'Temple of God'. Its golden plating was done by Maharaja Ranjit Singh. It is the holiest Gurudwara in Sikhism.

☛ When was the Golden Temple completed? → 1604 AD
☛ Which lake is the Golden Temple situated on? → Amritsar Lake

question: Which stone was mainly utilised in building the Chennakeshava Temple in Belur, India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Soapstone
Marble
Sandstone
Granite
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Soapstone

Explanation:
The Chennakeshava Temple in Belur, Karnataka, was built by the Hoysala Empire in the 12th century. The primary stone used in its construction is soapstone (steatite), a soft stone that allows intricate carving. This temple is famous for its detailed sculptures depicting deities, mythological scenes, and battles, all carved on soapstone. The Hoysala architecture heavily relies on soapstone, which hardens over time. The temple is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Hoysala temple complex.

☛ In which state is Chennakeshava Temple located? → Karnataka

☛ Who built the Chennakeshava Temple? → King Vishnuvardhana
☛ What was the capital of the Hoysala Empire? → Dwarasamudra (Halebidu)

question: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was a result of which global conference? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Earth Summit, 1992
Stockholm Conference
Paris Agreement
Kyoto Conference
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Earth Summit, 1992

Explanation:
The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was a key outcome of the Earth Summit (United Nations Conference on Environment and Development - UNCED) held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in 1992. This international treaty has three main objectives: the conservation of biological diversity, the sustainable use of its components, and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources. The Earth Summit was attended by leaders from over 150 countries and resulted in several landmark agreements, including the CBD and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The CBD entered into force on 29 December 1993 and currently has 196 parties.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Main objectives of CBD → Conservation, sustainable use, and benefit sharing
☛ Full name of Earth Summit → United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED)
☛ Number of parties to CBD → 196 (nearly all UN members)
☛ CBD entered into force → 29 December 1993
question_hi: कॉन्वेंशन ऑन बायोलॉजिकल डायवर्सिटी (CBD) किस वैश्विक सम्मेलन का परिणाम था? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 2)

स्टॉकहोम सम्मेलन
पेरिस समझौता
क्योटो सम्मेलन
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पृथ्वी शिखर सम्मेलन, 1992

Explanation:
जैव विविधता पर कन्वेंशन (CBD) 1992 में रियो डी जनेरियो में आयोजित पृथ्वी शिखर सम्मेलन (UNCED) का एक प्रमुख परिणाम था। यह एक अंतरराष्ट्रीय संधि है जिसका उद्देश्य जैव विविधता का संरक्षण, इसके घटकों का सतत उपयोग और आनुवंशिक संसाधनों से उत्पन्न लाभों का न्यायसंगत बंटवारा सुनिश्चित करना है। इस सम्मेलन में 150 से अधिक देशों के नेताओं ने भाग लिया और पर्यावरण तथा विकास से संबंधित कई समझौतों पर हस्ताक्षर किए, जिनमें CBD और जलवायु परिवर्तन पर संयुक्त राष्ट्र फ्रेमवर्क कन्वेंशन (UNFCCC) शामिल हैं। CBD 1993 में लागू हुआ और वर्तमान में इसके 196 पक्षकार हैं।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ CBD का प्रमुख उद्देश्य → जैव विविधता संरक्षण, सतत उपयोग और लाभ साझाकरण

question: Which of the following is an example of soft infrastructure? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Water pipelines
Public education
Bridges
Airports
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Public education

Explanation:
Soft infrastructure refers to the services and institutions essential for the smooth functioning of an economy, such as the education system, healthcare, and legal framework. Among the given options, water pipelines, bridges, and airports are examples of hard infrastructure, which are physical structures. In contrast, public education is a service-based system that contributes to human capital development and promotes economic growth. Therefore, public education is the correct example of soft infrastructure.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Example of hard infrastructure → Roads, dams, pipelines
☛ Example of soft infrastructure → Education, healthcare, banking
☛ Main purpose of soft infrastructure → Provide services and develop human resources
☛ Characteristic of hard infrastructure → Physical and tangible structures
☛ Broad impact of soft infrastructure → Economic growth and social welfare

question: _________ serves as the conventional base material for the art form known as Kalamkari. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Metal
Wood
Paper
Cloth
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cloth

Explanation:
Kalamkari is a traditional Indian hand-painting art form that uses cloth (cotton or silk) as the base material, with natural dyes applied using a bamboo pen. The term 'kalam' means pen and 'kari' means craftsmanship. Originating from Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, this art involves several steps: the cloth is washed, soaked, and treated before artisans draw intricate patterns. The cloth is then dyed with natural colors derived from plants and minerals. Thus, cloth is the essential base material for Kalamkari. Other materials like metal, wood, or paper are not used traditionally for this art form.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Base material for Kalamkari → Cloth
☛ Major Kalamkari centers → Srikakulam, Machilipatnam
☛ Dyes used in Kalamkari → Natural dyes (Indigo, Turmeric)
☛ Other name for Kalamkari → Peddamkuntla textile art
☛ Pen used in Kalamkari → Bamboo pen

question: Which of the following is a tribal dance of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (11/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: Which of the following programmes was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) in 2019 to improve air quality in 131 cities (non-attainment cities and million plus cities) across 24 states/UTs? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (11/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Swach Bayu Sarvekshan
National Association of Clean Air Agencies
Air Quality Forecasting System
National Clean Air Program
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Clean Air Program

Explanation:
The National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) was launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) in 2019 to improve air quality in 131 cities (non-attainment cities and million plus cities) across 24 states/UTs. The programme aims to reduce PM2.5 and PM10 levels by 20-30% by 2024, taking 2017 as the base year, later revised to 40%. Under NCAP, city-specific air quality management plans have been prepared, and a monitoring committee has been set up for implementation. It is a comprehensive initiative addressing both industrial and vehicular emissions, and promoting public awareness.

☛ What is the target reduction in PM levels under NCAP? → 20-30% by 2024 (later 40%)
☛ How many cities are covered under NCAP? → 131 cities (non-attainment and million plus)
☛ Which ministry implements NCAP? → MoEF&CC
☛ What is the full form of NCAP? → National Clean Air Programme

question: In which year did Andre-Marie Ampère publish his magnum opus ‘Mathematical Theory of Electrodynamic Phenomena Deduced Solely from Experiments’? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1833
1827
1818
1811
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1827

Explanation:

This work was groundbreaking as it established the relationship between electricity and magnetism, laying the foundation for electromagnetism. His name is immortalized in the SI unit of electric current 'Ampere' (A).

question: Which of the following schemes on Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) encourages entrepreneurs to set up CBG plants, produce and supply CBG to Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) for sale as automotive and industrial fuels?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants was adopted at a Conference of Plenipotentiaries in which year? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 2000
2002
2001
2003
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2001

Explanation:
The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants was adopted at a Conference of Plenipotentiaries held in Stockholm, Sweden, on 22-23 May 2001. It is a global treaty aimed at protecting human health and the environment from POPs (Persistent Organic Pollutants). The convention entered into force on 17 May 2004. Initially, it covered 12 key POPs, known as the Dirty Dozen, including chemicals like DDT, dioxins, and PCBs. India signed the convention in 2006. The convention is administered by UNEP (United Nations Environment Programme) and focuses on eliminating or reducing the production and use of POPs.
